en: Solid gallium metal melts into a liquid puddle just by holding it in your warm hand.
Dry ice is frozen carbon dioxide that skips the liquid phase and turns directly into gas through sublimation.
A mixture of cornstarch and water acts as a solid when punched but flows like a liquid when poured.
Water is one of the few substances that expands and becomes less dense when it freezes into solid ice.
Diamonds and the soft graphite in pencils are both made of the exact same pure carbon atoms.
The glowing substance inside a neon sign is actually a superheated fourth state of matter called plasma, not a regular gas.
Boiling red cabbage produces a purple juice that turns bright pink in acidic solutions and green in basic solutions.
Liquid nitrogen is so cold at minus 196 degrees Celsius that it can instantly freeze a peeled banana solid.
Milk is an emulsion, which is a unique mixture where tiny liquid fat droplets are permanently suspended in water.
Aerogel is a synthetic material composed of up to 99 percent air, making it one of the lightest solids.
The chewy base in modern bubblegum is actually a type of synthetic rubber polymer that your stomach cannot digest.
Every snowflake has six sides because water molecules naturally arrange themselves into hexagonal crystal lattices when they freeze.
